extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers and clinician-scientists applying for NIDDK K-series (career development) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of NIDDK K-series career development awards, listing each mechanism's eligibility, effort, duration, mentor requirement, and salary/cost limits, plus institute-specific policies and application deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored Research Scientist Development Award (K01) — eligibility & conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Ph.D., or comparable nonclinical degree, usually within 7 years of having received degree; minimum of 9 calendar months (75%) effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term: 3-5 years, not renewable. Mentor required. P.I. salary: Up to $90,000, plus fringe benefits. Read the full notice of funding opportunity for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored Clinical Scientist Development Award (K08) — eligibility & conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: M.D., or comparable clinical degree; minimum of 9 calendar months (75%) effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term: 3-5 years, not renewable. Mentor required. P.I. salary: Up to $100,000, plus fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored Patient-Oriented Research Career Development Award (K23) — eligibility & conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: M.D., or comparable clinical degree; minimum of 9 calendar months (75%) effort. Clinicians who interact directly with patients for their research (not just to fulfill departmental commitment) are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term: 3-5 years, not renewable. Mentor required. P.I. salary: Up to $100,000, plus fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentored Quantitative Research Career Development Award (K25) — eligibility & conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced degree in a quantitative area of science or engineering; minimum of 9 calendar months (75%) effort. Intended for non-biomedically trained Ph.D.s (e.g., mathematics, organic chemistry) moving into biomedical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term: 3-5 years, not renewable. Mentor required. P.I. salary: Up to $90,000, plus fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathway to Independence Award (K99/R00) — eligibility & structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ph.D., M.D., or equivalent research degree, with no more than 4 years of postgraduate research training; candidate needs only ~2 more years of mentored support before securing a U.S. faculty position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure: 2 years for the mentored K99; up to 3 years for the independent R00 phase. Citizenship: No citizenship requirement (K99/R00 open to citizens and non-citizens). Mentor required ONLY for the K99 phase. Funding: K99 = up to $75,000 (within the K99 total cost cap of $90,000/yr); R00 = at the institutional level, up to the NIH maximum (within the R00 total cost cap of $249,000/yr).

rubrics_metrics.name: MOSAIC Program (K99) — eligibility & structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Ph.D., M.D., or equivalent research degree, with no more than 4 years of postgraduate research training who needs only 2 more years of mentored support before securing a faculty position at a U.S. institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same structure and funding caps as K99/R00: 2 years mentored (K99) and up to 3 years R00; K99 = up to $75,000 (within K99 total cost cap $90,000/yr); R00 = institutional level up to NIH maximum (within R00 total cost cap $249,000/yr). No citizenship requirement. Mentor required for the mentored phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility requirements for mentored K awards (NIDDK)
rubrics_metrics.description: All mentored K awards require that the awardee meet several baseline conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: Be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident of the United States (does NOT apply to K99/R00); Be located at a U.S. institution; Have preliminary data on which to base a hypothesis-driven 3 to 5-year research project in an area of interest to the NIDDK; Have at least one mentor; Devote 9 calendar months (75 percent) effort to the K award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship policy across K mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Most K awards (K01, K08, K23, K25) are limited to U.S. citizens or permanent residents; K99/R00 and MOSAIC K99 are open to non-citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm citizenship and eligibility per mechanism in the full NOFO; general statement: 'Only US citizens or permanent residents are eligible for the K01, K08, K23, and K25; the K99/R00 is open to citizens or non-citizens.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum effort requirement and exception for urologic surgeons
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard minimum appointment is 9 calendar months (75%) effort devoted to the K award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: urologic surgeons may request less than a 9 calendar month (75%) commitment. Applicants must follow program-specific guidance for any allowed reduced effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration, renewability, and mentor requirement summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Most mentored K awards (K01, K08, K23, K25) are 3-5 years and are not renewable; mentored phase of K99 is 2 years with a subsequent independent R00 phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor required for mentored awards; explicit note that for K99 the mentor is required for the mentored K99 phase only. Consult NOFO for exact renewability and transition conditions for K99->R00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and cost limits by mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK specifies P.I. salary (and fringe) caps and total cost caps for different K mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: K01 and K25 P.I. salary up to $90,000 plus fringe; K08 and K23 up to $100,000 plus fringe. K99 = up to $75,000 (within K99 total cost cap of $90,000/yr); R00 = institutional level up to NIH maximum (within R00 total cost cap of $249,000/yr). Always verify current caps in the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIDDK policy on unsupported K mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK does not support the K02 award for more senior scientists and does not support the K24 award for midcareer scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking K02 or K24 support should note NIDDK will not fund those mechanisms and should consider alternative mechanisms or institutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental/related funding opportunity (limited competition R03)
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited competition small grant program (R03) is available to NIDDK K01, K08, and K23 awardees to provide additional, independent support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a separate small grant opportunity intended for current NIDDK K01/K08/K23 awardees; consult the specific R03 announcement for application rules and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines for new K applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDDK lists standard receipt dates for new K applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New Applications deadlines: February 12, June 12, October 12. Applicants must confirm current cycle dates and any changes in the NOFO or parent NIH schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must be located at a U.S. institution to receive NIDDK K award support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an eligibility condition for mentored K awards; verify institutional eligibility in the NOFO.
